_comment: tan-cli#664. `doctor`'s `data` values are host facts -- installed tool
versions, absolute paths, which checks even apply on this machine -- so
unlike every other entry `Bundle the envelope contract`
(.github/workflows/release.yml) folds into envelope-contract.json's
`envelopes` map, this one is not a byte golden. It pins the KEY SET
`alp-sdk-vscode` binds to (packages/alp-core/src/deps/planner.ts reads
`data.missingPrerequisites`; the debug troubleshooting panel renders
`checks[].fix` and `data.nextSteps` verbatim, alp-sdk-vscode#491) and
never a value.
Every value under `dataKeys` is a MACHINE TOKEN -- `"string"`, `"int"`,
`"string|null"` -- never a prose sentence: a consumer structurally
validating this contract must not have to parse English to learn a
shape. That is also why `checks` and `missingPrerequisites` are objects
rather than a single example dict / a description string: `checks`
splits into `requiredKeys` (present on every entry) and `optionalKeys`
(may be entirely absent, never null -- see `fix` below) so optionality
is a structural fact, not a note inside a type string; `missingPrerequisites`
is `{nullable, items}` so nullability is a structural fact too.
This file mixes three notations, all fixed by key name rather than a
declared meta-vocabulary -- a consumer hardcodes which is which, same as
this test does: (1) a LITERAL FIELD MAP, whose own keys ARE the emitted
field names one-for-one -- `summary` (`pass`/`warn`/`fail`) and
`dataKeys` itself (`generatedAt`/`summary`/`checks`/`missingPrerequisites`/
`nextSteps`); (2) a META-DESCRIPTOR, whose keys describe an ARRAY OF
OBJECTS the field actually carries on the wire, never a field of that
name -- `checks` (`requiredKeys`/`optionalKeys`, each itself a literal
field map of the per-entry shape) and `missingPrerequisites`
(`nullable`/`items`, `items` itself a literal field map of the per-entry
shape); (3) an ARRAY LITERAL, one example element long -- `nextSteps`:
`["string"]` means an array of strings, not a one-element array. `checks`
and `missingPrerequisites` are themselves arrays on the wire (`checks`
always, `missingPrerequisites` unless `null`) even though nothing in
their own key names says so -- that arrayness lives only in this
sentence and in `python/tests/conformance/test_doctor_contract_key_set.py`,
which asserts `isinstance(data["checks"], list)` and
`isinstance(missing_prereqs, list)` directly against the real envelope.
Enumerated 2026-08-12 by reading the ONE place `doctor`'s envelope is
assembled -- `python/tan/commands/doctor_cmd.py`'s `doctor()` (the
`data = {...}` literal), `Check.as_dict()` (the `checks[]` shape),
`summarise()`, `next_steps()`, and `tan.core.bootstrap.reported_missing`
(the `missingPrerequisites` shape) -- not curated by hand, and cross-
checked against a real `tan doctor --format json` run. `scope` was
added by tan-cli#549 after this issue's own worked example was written
and is included here because it is really on the wire today; the
issue's proposed shape predates it and omits it.
`status` is deliberately typed a free `string`, not an enum of its
current pass/warn/fail/unknown vocabulary: every consumer already passes
it through untouched, so a status value added later must survive the
trip rather than being coerced into today's list. The same reasoning is
applied to `scope`'s `host`/`project` vocabulary (`tan.core.doctor_scope`)
even though that one IS enforced server-side (`Check.__post_init__`) --
this file's promise is the key set, not the value vocabulary.
`fix` is OMITTED (never `null`) on a `checks[]` entry that passed, is
`unknown`, or otherwise carries no remediation -- `Check.as_dict()`'s
`skip_serializing_if`-equivalent, which is why it lives under
`checks.optionalKeys` rather than `checks.requiredKeys`.
`missingPrerequisites` is `null`, never `[]`, when `hostPrerequisites`
found nothing missing -- `reported_missing`'s own docstring: '`[]` is
NEVER a value here... One fact, one spelling.'
`data.nextSteps` is NOT guaranteed to equal the ordered list of non-null
`checks[].fix` values -- `next_steps()` (python/tan/commands/doctor_cmd.py)
additionally DEDUPES (one entry per distinct fix) and skips `pass`/
`unknown` checks even when they carry a `fix`, so the two arrays can and
do differ in length on a real run. Measured on the run this file was
enumerated against: 13 checks, 8 with a non-null `fix`, 7 `nextSteps`
entries (two checks shared the fix `tan bootstrap`, collapsed to one
`nextSteps` entry). This file promises only that both keys exist and
are arrays of strings.
`missingPrerequisites[]`'s four provenance keys -- `tier`, `licence`,
`sourceUrl`, `sizeBytes` -- were ADDED by tan-cli#1066 (additive, so no
MAJOR/MINOR break: nothing was renamed or dropped). They carry alp-sdk
v0.16.0's `metadata/bootstrap.json` `artifactProvenance` block
(alplabai/alp-sdk#1574), joined onto the entry by `tool` -- the identity
the entry already carried. They are REQUIRED keys, not optional ones,
and this is the deliberate difference from `checks[].fix` above: `fix`
is OMITTED when absent, while an unreported provenance field is an
explicit `null`. Absence here is a real, common, permanent answer --
`xz` and `7zip` declare no licence upstream, every `sizeBytes` is `null`
today, `python3-venv`/`west`/`zephyrSdk`/`setools`/`jlink` have no entry
at all, and an SDK predating v0.16.0 has no block -- so "not reported"
is a fact the consumer's consent screen renders, not a key it must
feature-detect. One shape for every SDK, which is why the same four keys
appear on `tan bootstrap`'s `missingPrerequisites[]` too (the two
commands share `tan.core.bootstrap.MissingPrerequisite.as_dict`).
`sourceUrl` is deliberately NOT alp-sdk's own spelling for that field,
which is `source`. tan renames it at this seam because the consumer that
asked for it (alp-sdk-vscode#467) already defines a `source` column as
what will actually RUN -- the install command, verbatim -- while
alp-sdk's `source` is the upstream project page, and what a user
installs is a brew bottle or an apt package, not the tarball behind it.
One name for two meanings would misinform the security reader that
screen exists for. `licence` keeps alp-sdk's own British spelling: same
fact, same name, no rename.
Renaming or dropping a key here is the same breaking wire change
`contract/README.md`'s frozen-issue-code rule describes for `issues[].code`:
bump the CLI MAJOR/MINOR, record it in CHANGELOG.md, and open the
matching alp-sdk-vscode issue.
`python/tests/conformance/test_doctor_contract_key_set.py` is the
lockstep check: it derives every required/optional key set (including
`checks[]`'s and `missingPrerequisites[]`'s) FROM this file -- never from
a hardcoded constant of its own -- runs a real `tan doctor --format
json`, and asserts the emitted key set equals the declared one exactly,
in both directions, so this file cannot drift silently from what the
command actually emits.
Unlike the sibling `issue-codes.json`, this file carries no top-level
`schemaVersion`. Neither file's own `schemaVersion` is read by any test
or script today (both are dead weight, verified by grep) -- but
`issue-codes.json` keeps its copy for symmetry with the bundle-wide
`"schemaVersion": 1` `envelope-contract.json` publishes (hardcoded in
`.github/workflows/release.yml`), since `issueCodes` is a frozen,
wire-compatibility-checked list (`contract/README.md`'s frozen-issue-code
rule) that could plausibly need its OWN version counter later if the
bundle-wide one ever stops being enough. This file's `args`/`dataKeys`
carry no comparable independent-versioning need, so it deliberately
carries no `schemaVersion` of its own rather than a second unread copy.
